title: What parameters must be configured for message flow from producer to broker to consumer?
shortTitle: What parameters must be configured for message flow from producer to broker to consumer?

s1_definition.profdef: Moving a record from a Kafka producer, through a broker, to a consumer requires a small set of mandatory parameters on each side plus a few that strongly affect correctness. On the producer you must set `bootstrap.servers`, `key.serializer`, and `value.serializer`, and you should consciously set `acks`. On the broker side the topic must exist with a chosen partition count and replication factor, and `min.insync.replicas` must be sane. On the consumer you must set `bootstrap.servers`, `key.deserializer`, `value.deserializer`, and `group.id`, and you should decide `auto.offset.reset` and `enable.auto.commit`.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of National Bank of India sending a transfer instruction. The producer is the branch clerk who must know the address of the central office (`bootstrap.servers`), how to write the form in a language the office understands (serializers), and how many confirmations to wait for (`acks`). The broker is the central mailroom that must have enough pigeonholes (partitions) and backup copies (replication) so a lost page never loses Rajesh's money. The consumer is the settlement team that must know the office address, how to read the form (deserializers), which team they belong to (`group.id`), and where to start reading if they are brand new (`auto.offset.reset`).

s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Moving a record from a Kafka producer, through a broker, to a consumer requires a small set of mandatory parameters on each side plus a few that strongly affect correctness. On the producer you must set `bootstrap.servers`, `key.serializer`, and `value.serializer`, and you should consciously set `acks`. On the broker side the topic must exist with a chosen partition count and replication factor, and `min.insync.replicas` must be sane. On the consumer you must set `bootstrap.servers`, `key.deserializer`, `value.deserializer`, and `group.id`, and you should decide `auto.offset.reset` and `enable.auto.commit`.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Think of National Bank of India sending a transfer instruction. The producer is the branch clerk who must know the address of the central office (`bootstrap.servers`), how to write the form in a language the office understands (serializers), and how many confirmations to wait for (`acks`). The broker is the central mailroom that must have enough pigeonholes (partitions) and backup copies (replication) so a lost page never loses Rajesh's money. The consumer is the settlement team that must know the office address, how to read the form (deserializers), which team they belong to (`group.id`), and where to start reading if they are brand new (`auto.offset.reset`).

**One line to remember:** Producer needs servers plus serializers plus acks, the broker needs partitions plus replication plus min.insync.replicas, and the consumer needs servers plus deserializers plus a group id.

sections.s2_technical:
On the producer, `bootstrap.servers` is a comma-separated list of broker host:port pairs used only for the initial connection; after that the producer discovers the full cluster. For example `props.put("bootstrap.servers", "broker1:9092,broker2:9092")` lets the producer survive one listed broker being down. The `key.serializer` and `value.serializer` convert your Java objects to bytes. For a money transfer you might use `props.put("value.serializer", "org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringSerializer")` when you send JSON, because Kafka itself only moves bytes and has no idea what a `TransferEvent` is.

The `acks` parameter decides durability. `acks=0` means fire and forget, `acks=1` means wait for the leader only, and `acks=all` means wait for all in-sync replicas. In banking you almost always use `props.put("acks", "all")` so a confirmed transfer is never silently lost. You pair this with `enable.idempotence=true`, which prevents duplicates on retry: `props.put("enable.idempotence", "true")`.

On the broker and topic side, the topic must exist with a partition count and replication factor. You create it with a command such as `kafka-topics --create --topic transfers --partitions 6 --replication-factor 3`. The broker-level `min.insync.replicas` works with `acks=all`: if you set `min.insync.replicas=2`, a write with `acks=all` only succeeds when at least two replicas have the data, so a single broker failure cannot lose a committed transfer.

On the consumer, `group.id` ties consumers into a group that shares partitions: `props.put("group.id", "settlement-service")`. The `key.deserializer` and `value.deserializer` turn bytes back into objects, for example `props.put("value.deserializer", "org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringDeserializer")`. The `auto.offset.reset` setting decides where a brand-new group starts when there is no committed offset: `props.put("auto.offset.reset", "earliest")` reads the whole backlog, while `latest` skips everything that arrived before the consumer started. Finally `enable.auto.commit` controls whether offsets commit automatically on a timer or whether you commit manually after processing; for exactly-once-ish behaviour you set `props.put("enable.auto.commit", "false")` and call `consumer.commitSync()` only after the transfer is persisted.

A senior nuance is that the serializer on the producer and the deserializer on the consumer must agree, because a `StringSerializer` producer and an Avro consumer will produce garbage. Another nuance is that `bootstrap.servers` should list at least two brokers so a single DNS or node failure does not stop the client from bootstrapping.
sections.s3_banking:
At National Bank of India, Rajesh (account SAV2001) transfers rent of fifty thousand rupees to Priya (account CUR3001). The transfer must flow from the branch application to the central Kafka cluster and then to the settlement service that actually moves money.

Problem 1 — the branch app does not know how to reach the cluster or how to encode the transfer. This is exactly what `bootstrap.servers` and the serializers solve: the producer learns where the brokers are and how to turn a `TransferEvent` object into bytes.

Problem 2 — the bank cannot afford to lose a confirmed transfer if one broker dies. This is exactly what `acks=all` together with a replication factor of three and `min.insync.replicas=2` solves: the write is only acknowledged once the data is safely on multiple machines.

Problem 3 — a brand-new settlement service must decide whether to process the old backlog or only new transfers. This is exactly what `group.id` and `auto.offset.reset` solve.

The code will show a producer that sets servers, serializers, and acks and sends a transfer, and a consumer that sets servers, deserializers, a group id, and manual commit, then processes the transfer and commits only after success.

```yaml
# application.yml
spring:
  kafka:
    bootstrap-servers: broker1:9092,broker2:9092,broker3:9092
    producer:
      acks: all
      properties:
        enable.idempotence: true
      key-serializer: org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringSerializer
      value-serializer: org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringSerializer
    consumer:
      group-id: settlement-service
      auto-offset-reset: earliest
      enable-auto-commit: false
      key-deserializer: org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringDeserializer
      value-deserializer: org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringDeserializer
```
sections.s4e_build:
```bash
# Build
mvn clean package -DskipTests

# Create the topic with partitions and replication
kafka-topics --bootstrap-server broker1:9092 --create \
  --topic transfers --partitions 6 --replication-factor 3 \
  --config min.insync.replicas=2

# Run the demo
java -cp target/kafka-flow-config-service-1.0.0.jar com.bank.kafkaflow.KafkaFlowDemo
```
sections.s5_journey:
Input data: a transfer of fifty thousand rupees from SAV2001 (Rajesh) to CUR3001 (Priya).

Step 1 — the producer reads `bootstrap.servers` and opens a connection to one listed broker, then discovers the full cluster and which broker leads the `transfers` partitions.

Step 2 — the producer serializes the `TransferEvent` using the configured `StringSerializer`, turning the Java object into JSON bytes. The key is the from-account, so Rajesh's events always hash to the same partition and stay ordered.

Step 3 — the producer sends the record with `acks=all`. The leader writes it, waits for the in-sync followers, and because `min.insync.replicas=2` at least two replicas must store it before success. Only then does the callback fire with a partition and offset.

Step 4 — the consumer reads `bootstrap.servers`, `group.id`, and the deserializers. Because it is a new group with `auto.offset.reset=earliest`, it starts at the beginning of each partition.

Step 5 — the consumer polls, deserializes the bytes back into readable JSON, applies the transfer to the ledger, and calls `commitSync()` only after the transfer succeeds, giving at-least-once delivery.

```
2026-10-24 21:20:01 [INFO] Published to partition 3 offset 48
2026-10-24 21:20:06 [INFO] Settling transfer: {"from":"SAV2001","to":"CUR3001","amount":50000}
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  Branch App: TransferEvent(SAV2001 → CUR3001, Rs.50000)
    │
    ▼
  Producer
    │ bootstrap.servers = broker1,broker2   (find the cluster)
    │ value.serializer  = String            (object → JSON bytes)
    │ acks = all, enable.idempotence = true (durable, no dup)
    │ key = "SAV2001"  → partition 3
    ▼
  Broker (leader of partition 3)
    │ write to leader
    ├─ replicate to follower A  (ISR)
    ├─ replicate to follower B  (ISR)
    │ min.insync.replicas = 2 satisfied → ACK
    ▼
  Topic transfers / partition 3 / offset 48
    │
    ▼
  Consumer (group.id = settlement-service)
    │ auto.offset.reset = earliest  (new group reads backlog)
    │ value.deserializer = String   (bytes → JSON)
    │ enable.auto.commit = false
    │ process → apply to ledger → commitSync()
    ▼
  Offset 48 committed for settlement-service
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
For a message to flow from producer to broker to consumer, each side needs a small set of parameters. On the producer, I always configure the bootstrap servers so the client can find the cluster, the key and value serializers so my Java objects become bytes, and the acknowledgement setting. In banking I set acknowledgements to all and enable idempotence so a confirmed transfer is durable and never duplicated on retry.

On the broker side, the topic must exist with a chosen partition count and replication factor, and I set the minimum in-sync replicas so that a write with all-acknowledgements only succeeds when the data is safely on more than one machine. This is what prevents a single broker crash from losing Rajesh's fifty thousand rupee transfer.

On the consumer, I configure the bootstrap servers, the key and value deserializers that must match the producer's serializers, and a group id that ties my consumers into one load-sharing group. I also decide the offset reset policy, which controls whether a brand-new group reads the whole backlog or only new messages, and I usually turn off automatic offset commit so I can commit only after the transfer is persisted.

In my National Bank of India project, this combination gave us durable, ordered, at-least-once delivery. The account number was the message key so all of one customer's events stayed ordered in the same partition, all-acknowledgements plus two in-sync replicas gave durability, and manual commit after writing to the ledger made sure we never acknowledged a transfer we had not actually applied.
